excel.importGuideTitle: Bulk inquiry import — how to fill in this file
excel.importRuleGrouping: One row = one piece of cargo. Rows sharing the same client reference are merged into one inquiry with several cargo lines; a different reference creates a separate inquiry.
excel.importRuleHeaderFirstRow: Service type, origin, destination and contact apply to the whole inquiry — fill them in on the first row of each reference only and leave them empty on the following rows.
excel.importRuleRequired: Columns marked * are mandatory (client ref., service type). In addition, origin and destination each need at least a country or a city.
excel.importRuleBusinessType: Pick the service type from the drop-down: TRUCK_LTL (truck LTL), TRUCK_FTL (truck FTL), LOCAL_DELIVERY (local delivery).
excel.importRuleAutoCalc: Volume and LDM are calculated automatically from the dimensions — leave them out. Dimensions are in centimetres, the weight is the weight per single piece in kilograms.
excel.importRuleLimit: Up to {{maxRows}} rows and {{maxInquiries}} inquiries per import; save the file in .xlsx format.
excel.importRulePreview: After uploading you get a preview with the validation result — confirm it before the import runs. A single error stops the whole batch.
excel.importExampleTitle: See the "Example" sheet: the first two rows are two pieces of the same inquiry, the third row is a separate inquiry.
excel.importErrUnreadable: The file could not be read — please make sure it is an .xlsx Excel file
excel.importErrMissingColumns: Missing required columns: {{columns}} — please use the current import template
excel.importErrNoData: The sheet contains no data rows
excel.importErrTooManyRows: {{actual}} data rows exceed the limit of {{max}} per import — please split the file
excel.importErrTooManyInquiries: {{actual}} inquiries exceed the limit of {{max}} per import — please split the file
excel.importErrRouteFrom: Origin needs at least a country or a city
excel.importErrRouteTo: Destination needs at least a country or a city
excel.importErrNoCargo: This inquiry has no cargo line — fill in at least the pieces or the dimensions on one row
excel.importErrQuantity: Pieces "{{value}}" must be a whole number greater than 0
excel.importWarnEmail: The email address does not look valid
excel.importWarnDuplicate: An inquiry with client ref. {{ref}} already exists — please check this is not a duplicate import
excel.importWarnHeaderConflict: Differs from "{{kept}}" on the first row of this inquiry — "{{ignored}}" on this row is ignored
excel.importWarnBusinessType: Service type not recognised and ignored — use TRUCK_LTL / TRUCK_FTL / LOCAL_DELIVERY
excel.importWarnTransportType: Dedicated/shared not recognised and ignored — use FTL (dedicated truck) or LTL (shared truck)
excel.importWarnVehicleLength: Vehicle length not recognised and ignored — pick one from the template dropdown, or just type the length (e.g. 13.6)
excel.importWarnVehicleLengthIgnored: Vehicle length only applies to a dedicated truck (FTL); the value in this row was ignored
excel.importRuleTransportType: "Dedicated/shared" and "Vehicle length" only apply to truck services: enter FTL for a dedicated truck, LTL for a shared one. Vehicle length is only used for dedicated trucks and is ignored for shared ones. Both columns are optional.
excel.ldImportGuideTitle: Local delivery bulk import · How to fill in
excel.ldRuleGrouping: One row = one package. Rows are grouped into inquiries by "Container no.", and within a container into individual deliveries by "Delivery ref.". So all deliveries out of one container go into a single sheet.
excel.ldRuleHeaderFirstRow: Container-level details (pickup address, sender contact) only need to be filled in on the container's first row; delivery-level details (delivery address, receiver) only on that delivery's first row. Different values on later rows raise a warning and the first row wins.
excel.ldRuleRequired: Columns marked * are required: container no. and delivery ref. Every delivery needs at least one cargo row (quantity or dimensions).
excel.ldRuleAutoCalc: Volume, LDM and the per-delivery and per-container totals are all calculated automatically — leave them out.
excel.ldRuleLimit: Up to {{maxRows}} rows and {{maxContainers}} containers per import.
excel.ldErrTooManyContainers: Up to {{max}} containers per import, this file has {{actual}}
excel.ldWarnDuplicateContainer: Container {{no}} already has an inquiry in the system — please check this is not a duplicate import
excel.importErrDateFormat: {{field}} has an invalid format, use a date like 2026-09-01
excel.orderImportRuleOneRow: One row = one order. As many data rows as you fill in, that many orders will be created.
excel.orderImportRuleProduct: This template only imports "{{product}}" orders. For other products download the matching template from the system — each product needs different fields.
excel.orderImportRuleRequired: Columns marked * are mandatory: {{columns}}. Other columns may be left empty; our operations team will complete them later.
excel.orderImportRuleDate: Dates can be written as 2026-09-01 or 01.09.2026, or entered as a real Excel date.
excel.orderImportRuleNumber: Weight, volume and pieces must be numbers without units. Both "." and "," work as decimal separator; pieces must be a whole number.
excel.orderImportRuleLimit: Up to {{maxRows}} rows per import; please save the file as .xlsx.
excel.orderImportRulePreview: After upload you get a preview with validation results. Nothing is imported until you confirm — and a single error blocks the whole batch.
excel.orderImportRuleStatus: Imported orders behave like manually created ones: they start as "Pending review". Importing does not mean the shipment is accepted yet.
excel.orderImportErrBusinessType: Please specify the transport product to import (TRUCK_LTL / TRUCK_FTL / LOCAL_DELIVERY)
excel.orderImportErrDate: {{field}} "{{value}}" is not a valid date, use 2026-09-01 or 01.09.2026
excel.orderImportWarnDuplicate: "{{value}}" is the same as in row {{row}} — ignore this if it is intentional
excel.orderImportRuleCustomerRef: "Client reference" is your own order/reference number, so both sides can match records later. It may be left empty. The same reference may span several orders (e.g. one shipment split across two containers).
excel.orderImportRulePickupFtl: The pickup country/postcode/city/address is the **container pickup location**. Leave it empty for the normal case (pickup at the discharge port); fill it in only when we should collect from a specific terminal or your own warehouse.
